metadata.Info: RuneArt is dedicated to initiating a new chapter for Fine Art on Bitcoin. Created by artists for art lovers, we aim to make art accessible by allowing multiple collectors to participate in a single piece through a community-driven experience. Re-imagining the use of fungible tokens for networked art. By merging Rune tokens and Ordinals, we have developed a unique format where each 1-of-1 artwork is decentralized into collectible ‘ArtNodes’ - individual Rune tokens that empower collectors to be stewards and shape the future of art on Bitcoin. Our mission is to grow the Bitcoin Fine Art ecosystem, while fostering deeper connections between collectors and artists.

metadata.Title: Timestamps
metadata.Description: The debut collaborative Rune Art collection featuring renowned artists, each contributing a series of 10 unique 1-of-1 artworks, all revolving around the concept of time. Every artwork is linked to a single Rune token ticker with a supply of 100 collectable tokens - ‘ArtNodes’. Each 'TIMESTAMPS' artist explores the intersection of Bitcoin and the concept of TIME through the lens of their art. To represent the stylistic variety of art on-chain, it was important to select artists with diverse backgrounds and aesthetics. Fun Fact: Satoshi Nakamoto often referred to blockchain as ‘Timechain’ - being that decentralized timestamping is a fundamental element of the technology itself. As a gesture to this, the ‘TIMESTAMPS’ collection explores how Bitcoin can be used as a medium on a deeper level, exploring the concepts of timestamping, distribution and what it means to create art on-chain.

metadata.Bio: Andrea Chiampo, an Italian London-based contemporary artist and concept designer, is known for his eerie, surreal art that blends otherworldly landscapes with fantastical creatures. With a background in Industrial Design and experience with major studios like 20th Century Fox, Netflix, and Disney, Andrea’s personal series FUTURED PAST captures the intersection of past, present, and future in mesmerizing detail.

Creating art for the Internet since 1995, Auriea Harvey is known for her net art, video games, and digital/physical hybrid sculptures. She blends digital and handmade techniques to create works which play between mythology and autobiography, art history and imagination. Her impressive portfolio includes pieces in prestigious collections like the Whitney Museum and the Rf.C Collection. She has exhibited at renowned venues such as Centre Pompidou, the Victoria & Albert Museum, and the New Museum.

Burst is an anonymous cryptoartist known for his post-neoexpressionist style, creating futuristic, hybrid-organic artworks that blend digital and physical media. His multi- and mixed-media works, supported by video, animation, and painting, explore transformative processes of the human psyche in the digital age, often using repeating motives as a form of intuitive code.

Gordon Berger is a pioneer of the Crypto Art movement. Since 2011 he has been at the forefront of blockchain and has dedicated his career to merging algorithms with traditional techniques. Actively contributing to the growth of digital art on-chain, from his groundbreaking TEDx talk on NFTs and presenting an AI project to NASA in 2018, to creating one of the earliest generative art projects on Ethereum and inscribing art on Bitcoin. His work is a testament to the evolution of art and its networked effects in the digital age.

Dr. Ivona Tau, a generative A.I. artist from Vilnius, blends neural networks and code to create experimental photography and motion painting that evoke deep emotions. With a Ph.D. in A.I. and extensive experience in both photography and A.I. research, her work has been featured at major events like Art Basel and is held in prominent collections such as ZMK Museum of Contemporary Art.

A multidisciplinary artist and founder, Toomuchlag blends the dystopian with the celestial, creating vibrant works inspired by literature, cinema, and gaming. His interactive NFTs, like Satoshi’s Coin, use blockchain-native mechanics to offer unique experiences, and his work has been showcased globally from London to Beijing and auctioned at Christie's NY.

Orkhan Mammadov is a visionary new media artist from Azerbaijan, renowned for blending Middle Eastern cultural heritage with cutting-edge art-making methods. His work, which gained international attention after representing Azerbaijan at the 2019 Venice Biennale, uses AI and machine learning to reimagine Islamic patterns and traditional art forms into captivating digital and physical sculptures.

metadata_items.metadata: "I've been working on a new electronic cash system that's fully peer-to-peer, with no trusted third party." Satoshi 10/31/08
"A purely peer-to-peer version of electronic cash would allow online payments to be sent directly from one party to another without going through a financial institution.” Satoshi 10/31/08
“Governments are good at cutting off the heads of a centrally controlled networks like Napster, but pure P2P networks like Gnutella and Tor seem to be holding their own.” Satoshi 11/06/08
“It might make sense just to get some in case it catches on. If enough people think the same way, that becomes a self fulfilling prophecy.” Satoshi 01/17/09
“Banks must be trusted to hold our money and transfer it electronically, but they lend it out in waves of credit bubbles with barely a fraction in reserve.” Satoshi 01/11/09

“I’ve developed a new open source P2P e-cash system called Bitcoin. It’s completely decentralized, with no central server or trusted parties, because everything is based on crypto proof instead of trust.” Satoshi 02/11/09
“It is a global distributed database, with additions to the database by consent of the majority.” Satoshi 02/18/09
“For greater privacy, it’s best to use bitcoin addresses only once.” Satoshi 11/25/09
“The possibility to be anonymous or pseudonymous relies on you not revealing any identifying information about yourself in connection with the bitcoin addresses you use.” Satoshi 11/25/09
“Can nodes tell which bitcoin addresses belong to which IP addresses? No.” Satoshi 11/25/09

“Being open source means anyone can independently review the code. If it was closed source, nobody could verify the security. I think it’s essential for a program of this nature to be open source.” Satoshi 12/10/09
“I’m sure that in 20 years there will either be very large transaction volume or no volume.” Satoshi 02/14/10
“If you don’t believe it or don’t get it, I don’t have the time to try to convince you, sorry.” Satoshi 01/29/10
“In a few decades when the reward gets too small, the transaction fee will become the main compensation for nodes.” Satoshi 02/14/10
“How does everyone feel about the B symbol with the two lines through the outside? Can we live with that as our logo?” Satoshi 02/26/10
“The nature of Bitcoin is such that once version 0.1 was released, the core design was set in stone for the rest of its lifetime.” Satoshi 06/17/10
“Lost coins only make everyone else’s coins worth slightly more. Think of it as a donation to everyone.” Satoshi 06/21/10
“When someone tries to buy all the world’s supply of a scarce asset, the more they buy the higher the price goes.” Satoshi 07/09/10

“I anticipate there will never be more than 100K nodes, probably less. It will reach an equilibrium where it's not worth it for more nodes to join in. The rest will be lightweight clients, which could be millions.” Satoshi 07/14/10
“The heat from your computer is not wasted if you need to heat your home.” Satoshi 08/09/10
